title: Generation-first story-title authoring and trends vocabulary
summary: Two content-quality increments that the cron coding agent (Codex/Claude Code) relies on, since the environment has no usable LLM API and authoring happens through the report:draft to quality:review to repair-contract loop. First, after Stage D moved the public unit to per-story collapsibles, deterministic templated story-title variants such as the entity-plus-generic-verb-plus-generic-noun shape were escaping both the selection-time templated-title predicate and the review phrase list, so they shipped as boilerplate. The review template-narrative detector now covers those title families and routes them to public_editorial_rewrite so the agent authors them from each story's own sources; facts, links, and dates stay protected. Second, the trend engine already counts controlled-vocabulary occurrences across sections, so emerging engineering concepts produced no trend pressure purely from a vocabulary gap; a harness-engineering controlled topic was added so harness/context-engineering/long-running-agent terms register across sections without any engine or threshold change. The single authoritative editorial asset records the generation-first authoring directive as a Bad Case and history entry.

validation_commands: node --test tests/unit.test.js tests/story-authoring.test.js tests/content-contract.test.js tests/page-check-tiering.test.js tests/source-coverage.test.js tests/trends.test.js

lessons.lesson: Story authoring coverage was a brittle phrase list; deterministic templated titles escaped it after the Stage D layout change.
lessons.evidence: A story titled with the generic update-agent-and-developer-tools template produced no public_editorial_rewrite task before the change; after extending the review template-narrative detector to those title families, both observed variants route to authoring while a concrete title stays out.
lessons.recommended_action: When the public rendering unit changes, re-check that the deterministic generator's prose families are still routed to the agent authoring loop, not just a fixed phrase list.

lessons.lesson: Emerging trend topics failed to surface because of a vocabulary gap, not an engine limit.
lessons.evidence: The trend engine already counts occurrences across main_items, hot_blogs, builder_observations, and github_trending; adding a harness-engineering controlled topic made the concept register across sources with no threshold change.
lessons.recommended_action: Treat missing trend pressure on a known-hot concept as a controlled-vocabulary gap first; extend config/trends.json before touching the scoring engine.

lessons.lesson: The harness task-file validator strips inline code before checking required sections.
lessons.evidence: Feedback Ledger Review and Retrospective Plan failed validation because their trigger tokens were inside backticks; moving the keywords into plain prose passed the gate.
lessons.recommended_action: Put required section trigger words (feedback-ledger, project_iteration, retrospectives index) in plain text, not inline code, in tasks/current-task.md.

followups.action: Have the daily runner repair-contract step actually backfill authored story narrative on every run, so generation-first prose ships without manual agent intervention.
Deferred this round: cross-source co-occurrence scoring, GitHub Trending API field enrichment, and a curated first-party X handle list.
